content: 1. Psychological interventions, such as cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), should be offered as a treatment option for individuals experiencing emotional disorders. 2. Antidepressants may be considered for adolescents with moderate to severe depressive disorders when psychosocial interventions have been shown to be ineffective. 3. The use of antidepressants, including tricyclic antidepressants and selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), can be considered for children aged 6–12 years who are diagnosed with depressive episodes or disorders. 4. Suicide prevention is a global priority, as outlined in the World Health Organization's 2014 report, which emphasizes the need for comprehensive strategies to address this critical issue. 5. Pharmacological interventions may be utilized for the management of somatoform disorders in children and adolescents, as per WHO guidelines. 6. The WHO guideline on school health services provides a framework for delivering quality health services in educational settings to promote the well-being of students. 7. The WHO, in collaboration with the OECD and the World Bank, emphasizes the importance of delivering quality health services as a global imperative for achieving universal health coverage. 8. Guidelines for iodine thyroid blocking have been developed to assist in planning and responding to radiological and nuclear emergencies. 9. The WHO's health emergency and disaster risk management framework provides guidance on preparedness and response strategies for health emergencies. 10. Public health measures in schools during the COVID-19 pandemic, including adjustments to social and health protocols, are outlined in WHO recommendations. 11. The WHO has issued rapid advice guidelines on the use of personal protective equipment during outbreaks of filovirus diseases, such as Ebola. 12. Managing epidemics requires a comprehensive understanding of key facts about major deadly diseases, as detailed in WHO resources. 13. Guidelines for investigating and controlling foodborne disease outbreaks have been established to ensure effective public health responses. 14. The WHO has developed a guideline for responding to meningitis outbreaks in sub-Saharan Africa, emphasizing timely and coordinated action. 15. Recommendations for responding to measles outbreaks in high-mortality settings focus on reducing the impact of the disease through targeted interventions. 16. Cholera outbreak response guidelines include assessing the effectiveness of current measures and improving preparedness for future outbreaks. 17. Initial steps for managing acute diarrhea outbreaks are outlined in WHO resources to guide public health responses. 18. School-based interventions aimed at reducing suicide and suicide attempts among young people are supported by evidence-based WHO recommendations. 19. Resources for teachers and school staff on preventing suicide provide practical guidance for creating supportive environments for students. 20. The prevention of allergy and allergic asthma is addressed in WHO/WAO recommendations, based on a 2002 meeting in Geneva. 21. Preventing violence through the development of safe, stable, and nurturing relationships between children and their caregivers is a key focus of WHO guidelines. 22. The Alcohol, Smoking, and Substance Involvement Screening Test (ASSIST) manual provides guidance for primary care providers on addressing substance use. 23. WHO policies and plans for child and adolescent mental health emphasize the importance of comprehensive strategies to address mental health needs. 24. Preventive chemotherapy guidelines aim to control soil-transmitted helminth infections in at-risk populations. 25. Alternative mass drug administration regimens to eliminate lymphatic filariasis are outlined in WHO guidelines. 26. WHO recommendations on digital interventions for health system strengthening highlight the role of technology in improving healthcare delivery. 27. The Digital Implementation Investment Guide (DIIG) provides a framework for integrating digital interventions into health programs. 28. A shared language for describing the use of digital technology in health is essential for effective communication and implementation. 29. A framework for national health policies, strategies, and plans has been developed to guide countries in achieving health goals. 30. The WHO handbook on strategizing national health in the 21st century offers practical tools for developing effective health strategies. 31. The AA-HA. manual facilitates the development of national adolescent health strategies and plans, emphasizing accelerated action for adolescent health. 32. The WHO consultative group on equity and universal health coverage highlights the importance of making fair choices to achieve health equity. 33. Evidence-informed deliberative processes are essential for priority setting in universal health coverage, beyond just cost-effectiveness analysis. 34. Mapping multiple criteria for health intervention priority setting provides decision-makers with tools to make informed choices. 35. A global review of policies, standards, and guidelines for health-promoting schools underscores the importance of creating supportive educational environments. 36. Declarations of interest for individuals involved in WHO guideline development are documented and assessed to ensure transparency and integrity in the process.
